items.title: Roblox confirms no adult content used in AI training after scraping Open3DLab data
items.en_title: Roblox confirms no adult content used in AI training after scraping Open3DLab data
items.en_oneliner: Roblox confirmed no adult content was used in AI training, admitting its AI agent went out of control while scraping Open3DLab data.

items.title: Subnautica 2 dev thinks early access teams should worry less about adding features that are "very ugly, incomplete, or prototype"
items.en_title: Subnautica 2 dev thinks early access teams should worry less about adding features that are "very ugly, incomplete, or prototype"
items.en_oneliner: Subnautica 2's creative director advised early access teams not to fear shipping ugly, incomplete features, as the sooner players play, the sooner direction can adjust from feedback.

items.title: Maya Workflow Toolkit for Blender
items.en_oneliner: The new Maya Workflow Toolkit plugin makes Blender feel like Maya, suited to artists used to Maya who want to switch to Blender.

items.title: Sensor Tower: Half of ad impressions in casual games come from ad networks, while strategy titles focus on social platforms
items.en_title: Sensor Tower: Half of ad impressions in casual games come from ad networks, while strategy titles focus on social platforms
items.en_oneliner: Sensor Tower data shows casual and strategy games split sharply on ad channels — half of casual ad impressions come from ad networks, while strategy titles lean on social platforms.

items.title: How to run an indie game studio: Part 5, Better meetings
items.en_title: How to run an indie game studio: Part 5, Better meetings
items.en_oneliner: The fifth piece in the running an indie studio series focuses on meetings, explaining how efficient meetings connect goals, agendas, and quarterly rhythm.

items.title: Valve weighs in on Next Fest AI cloning phenomenon
items.en_title: Valve weighs in on Next Fest AI cloning phenomenon
items.en_oneliner: Valve addressed the phenomenon of AI rapidly cloning games on Steam, acknowledging the problem exists while placing more of the prevention burden on developers themselves.
